==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|larn||Northumbrian}} * {{alt|en|learne||obsolete}} ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:lernen>}} From {{inh|en|enm|lernen|t=to learn", also, "to teach"}}, from {{inh|en|ang|leornian|t=to learn", rarely also, "to teach}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*liʀnōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*lizaną}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro||*(le-)lóys-e}}, stative from the root {{m|ine-pro|*leys-|t=track, furrow, trace, trail}}. The spelling with ⟨ea⟩ is of {{w|Early Modern English}} origin and reflects a lengthening of {{IPAchar|/ɛ~e/}} to {{IPAfont|/eː/}} before {{IPAchar|/rn/}} in Late Old English or Early Middle English, then later lowering to {{IPAchar|/ɛː/}}; the modern pronunciation reflects still later reshortening. The dialect form with {{IPAfont|/ɑː/}} reflects the Middle English pronunciation which either retained the short {{IPAchar|/ɛ/}} or reshortened it earlier, enabling the a development to {{IPAchar|/a/}} before {{IPAchar|/r/}} which yielded modern {{IPAfont|/ɑː/}}. Cognate with {{cog|ofs|lernia}}, {{m|ofs|lerna|t=to learn}}, {{cog|gml|lernen|t=to learn", also, "to teach}}, {{cog|dum|leernen|t=to learn", also, "to teach}} (whence {{cog|nl|lernen|t=to study scripture}}), {{cog|de|lernen|t=to learn}}. See also {{m|en|lore}} and {{m|en|lear#Verb}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|lûn|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/lɜːn/}} * {{enPR|lûrn|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/lɝn/}} * {{audio|en|en-uk-to learn.ogg|a=UK|text=to learn}} * {{audio|en|en-us-learn.ogg|a=US}} * {{enPR|lä(r)n|a=dialectal}}, {{IPA|en|/lɑː(ɹ)n/}} {{q|see {{m|en|larn}}}} * {{IPA|en|/lɛːrn/|/lɛrn/|a=Early Modern}}{{R:en:Dobson:1957|II|8|470|passage=''Learn'' has ''ę̄'' in Levins (beside ''ĕ''), Hart (beside ''ĕ''), Bullokar, and Cooper, and ''ĕ'' in Robinson, Gil, Hodges, Poole, Coles, Brown, and ''RS''. }} * {{rhymes|en|ɜː(ɹ)n|s=1}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb|+|+|+,~t}} # To [[acquire]], or attempt to acquire [[knowledge]] or an ability to do something. #:''It's time Dad '''learn'''ed (how) to change the oil in the car''. #:''In my latest job, I've '''learn'''t to keep my mouth shut more than in the last one''. #:''Toddlers '''learn''' to walk at around one year old.'' #* {{RQ:Cowper Task |passage=a school in which he '''learns''' sly circumvention}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1988|author=Mark Andre Peter Loranc|title=A Study of the Ionospheric Signature of Ion Supply from the Ionosphere to the Magnetosphere|page=iv|text=I have '''learned''' far more from them about how to be a scientist than they realize. Above all else, they taught me the virtues of proper waterfowl alignment.|chapter=Acknowledgements|genre=PhD dissertation|location=University of Texas at Dallas}} #*: Every day I '''learn''' more about this great city. # To [[attend]] a course or other [[educational]] activity. #* {{RQ:Defoe Robinson Crusoe|passage=For, as he took delight to introduce me, I took delight to '''learn.'''}} # To gain knowledge from a bad [[experience]] so as to [[improve]]. #: {{ux|en|'''learn''' from one's mistakes}} # To [[study]]. #: {{ux|en|I '''learn''' medicine.}} #: {{ux|en|They '''learn''' psychology.}} # To come to [[know]]; to become [[inform]]ed of; to [[find out]]. #: {{ux|en|He just '''learned''' that he will be sacked.}} # {{lb|en|now only in|_|non-standard speech|and|dialects}} To [[teach]]. #: {{ux|en|Give him a [[clip]] round the ear. That'll '''learn''' him!}} #* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|10.9|2|VIII|ix|passage=And whan she had serched hym
she fond in the bottome of his wound that therin was poyson
And soo she heled hym{{...}}
and therfore Tramtrist cast grete loue to la beale Isoud
for she was at that tyme the fairest mayde and lady of the worlde
And there Tramtryst '''lerned''' her to harpe
and she beganne to haue grete fantasye vnto hym}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Much Ado About Nothing Q|act=IV|scene=i|sig=F3|verso=1|page=49|passage=Sweete Prince, you '''learne''' me noble thankfulnes: {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Cymbeline|act=I|scene=v|page=373|column=1|passage=Haue I not bene
Thy Pupill long? Haſt thou not '''learn'd''' me how
To make Perfumes?}} #* {{RQ:Bunyan Christian Behaviour|chapter=Touching Parents|page=56|passage={{...}} ''Take heed of filling their'' {{quote-gloss|''i.e.'', children's}} ''heads with VVhimzies, and unprofitable Notions''; for this vvill ſooner '''learn''' them to be malepert and proud, than ſober and humble.}} #* {{RQ:Twain Tom Sawyer|page=200|passage=But we’ll play Robin Hood—it’s noble fun.
